push.body:
buddskees, I've coached a lot of games, and a 10.0 like that one still gives me goosebumps.

+ 2 key passes, the most you've made for us. That's what I call neighborly football.
+ PhogsToffees owes you a milkshake for those passes.
+ 10.0 is your best rating in 5 matches. Frame it.
+ 2.3 better than usual. That's a staircase, and you're climbing it.
+ 10.0, your best match performance. Bottle it.

WORK ON
- Only 0 passes (down from your usual 13). Here's the trick: Show for it. Move into the passing lane and ask for the ball instead of hiding behind your marker. Steady does it.
- No tackles attempted. Bread and butter: Know your runner before the cross comes in. A quick look over the shoulder saves a goal.
- Same on-ball involvement trouble for you and tuxedo_slide. Buddy up: make triangles, 1-2 touch.

Pre-match routine: Check away, then check back. A two-yard feint buys you the space to receive.

Before you go, buddskees: The ball will find the player who wants it. Want it.

That's how it's done. More of that, please. - Coach Lasso

tuxedo_slide, a 7.0. Think of it like a flat tire. Annoying, fixable, and we've got a spare.

push.title: W 4-1 vs Real Munch | You: 6.4 (4th worst match performance)
push.body:
BellyTb1, a 6.4. If you ever wonder whether I've got your back, the answer is always.

DID WELL
+ 4-1 win. Three points in the cupboard.

WORK ON
- Won 0 of 3 tackles (down from your usual 36%). Here's how: Get low and side-on. Square-on defenders get nutmegged. Patience, partner.
- 59% passing (13 of 22, down from your usual 79%). For next time: Before the killer ball, check: is my runner onside, moving, and unmarked? Two out of three isn't enough.
- Rating came in 0.5 below what your on-ball stats earned. Start here: Your rating came in lower than your stats say, and that gap is off-ball: positioning, interceptions, blocks.
- Both you and tuxedo_slide dipped on tackle timing. Lean on each other: one presses, one covers.
- 1.4 under your typical rating. Short memory, long season.

Backyard drill: Delay, deny, then dictate. Jockey goal-side and only commit when their touch gets heavy.

Remember, BellyTb1: The comeback is always more fun than the setback.

Stay curious about your game. - Coach Lasso
